title: School guidance support and growth in mathematics discourse feedback skills: a three-wave longitudinal mediation study
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether perceived school guidance support is associated with growth in students’ mathematics discourse feedback skills, and whether that association operates through two time-ordered mediators: major decision-making self-efficacy and feedback literacy behavior. The authors frame the problem as a challenge of how contextual support helps students not only receive feedback, but also use it productively in classroom mathematical dialogue.

The study used a three-wave longitudinal design with Chinese senior high school students in Hebei, China. Students reported school guidance support at Time 1, major decision-making self-efficacy at Time 2, feedback literacy behavior at Time 3, and mathematics discourse feedback skills across all three waves. The sample included 2,120 adolescents from three senior high schools, with data collected at approximately three-month intervals. Analyses used longitudinal structural equation modeling with controls for prior skill levels and demographic covariates.

Results showed that higher perceived school guidance support predicted stronger later mathematics discourse feedback skills both directly and indirectly. The association was mediated by major decision-making self-efficacy and by feedback literacy behavior, and a sequential pathway from guidance support to self-efficacy to feedback literacy behavior to mathematics discourse feedback skills was also supported. The authors conclude that school guidance services may support disciplinary feedback skill development by strengthening students’ confidence in decision-making and by fostering habitual feedback-seeking and feedback-use behaviors.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed longitudinal correlational study with three waves, measurement invariance testing, and structural equation modeling. However, it is not an experimental or quasi-experimental intervention study, so causal credibility is limited despite strong statistical controls.
impact_tier_rationale: The reported effects are positive and moderately sized in standardized terms, but they concern student self-report constructs rather than direct achievement or implementation outcomes. The study is informative for theory and school guidance practice, yet it does not test an education technology or AI intervention and has unclear direct operational impact.

finding.finding_summary: This three-wave longitudinal study found that higher T1 school guidance support predicted higher T3 mathematics discourse feedback skills, controlling for prior skills and demographics. In the fully adjusted sequential mediation model, the total standardized effect was β=0.371, with a remaining direct effect of β=0.112 and a significant indirect pathway via major decision-making self-efficacy and feedback literacy behavior (β=0.054).
finding.measure: High School Students’ Mathematics Discourse Feedback Skills Scale (MDFSS), measured at T1, T2, and T3
finding.effect_size: β=0.371 total; β=0.112 direct; β=0.054 sequential indirect

finding.finding_summary: School guidance support was strongly associated with greater major decision-making self-efficacy at T2, which then predicted later mathematics discourse feedback skills. In the single-mediator model, the path from guidance support to self-efficacy was β=0.476, and the indirect effect through self-efficacy was β=0.126 (95% CI [0.107, 0.142]).
finding.study_size: n=2120 at T1; longitudinal SEM on retained sample
finding.confidence_interval: 95% CI [0.434, 0.512] for guidance→self-efficacy; [0.107, 0.142] for indirect effect

finding.finding_summary: Feedback literacy behavior was positively associated with later mathematics discourse feedback skills, and it partially explained the effect of school guidance support. In the sequential mediation model, guidance support predicted feedback literacy behavior (β=0.213), and the indirect pathway via feedback literacy behavior was significant (β=0.059, 95% CI [0.034, 0.088]); the full sequential chain through self-efficacy and feedback literacy was also significant (β=0.054).
finding.measure: Feedback Literacy Behavior Scale and MDFSS
finding.study_size: n=1938 at T3 in the final wave; structural model based on longitudinal sample
finding.effect_size: β=0.213 path; β=0.059 indirect; β=0.054 sequential indirect
finding.confidence_interval: 95% CI [0.034, 0.088] for feedback-literacy indirect; [0.037, 0.076] for sequential indirect
